data.title: Aggie Green Fund Showcase
data.description:
Want to see the real-world impact of the Aggie Green Fund? You’re invited to the AGF Project Showcase, where past grant recipients will share how their projects are making Texas A&M a more sustainable place.

This is your opportunity to hear directly from the students, faculty, and staff who are turning innovative ideas into reality. You’ll learn about a range of projects and from every corner of our campus.

Join us to get inspired, ask questions, have a snack, and celebrate the incredible work being done to create a greener campus.

data.title: Internship Applications Open
data.summary:
The goal of the Office of Sustainability & Campus Enrichment’s Internship Program is to bring undergraduate students from a variety of backgrounds and perspectives together to create a dynamic team that works to create a culture of sustainability at Texas A&M University. Interns work together to increase awareness and education about the three pillars of sustainability: environmental, economic, and social. The team focuses on educating the campus community about topics such as: energy and water use, transportation, food services, construction and built environment, purchasing, recycling, and social sustainability through the development of outreach initiatives and event coordination. Additionally, interns support assessment and planning efforts prioritized by the office.

The Internship Program is open to any TAMU undergraduate student and all majors are encouraged to apply because true sustainability must be an interdisciplinary enterprise.

Applications are open October 5, 2026 – November 2, 2026 at https://sustainability.tamu.edu/team/employment.html

data.title: Under the Weather: Understanding Texas Disaster Risk and Resilience
data.summary:
Campus Sustainability Month Talk by Office of Sustainability & Campus Enrichment Student Interns.

This event will take place via zoom, click the link below to register.
data.description: Texas is one of the most disaster affected areas in the United States, in terms of both frequency and cost of disaster occurrences. Explore two of the most devastating Texas disasters: Hill Country Floods and Gulf Coast hurricanes to understand their causes, costs, and recovery. Through these case studies, learn about how rapid climate change increases the risk of disasters and why building community resilience is the best way to move forward.

data.title: Quality over Quantity: The Impacts of Humanitarian Aid
data.summary:
Campus Sustainability Month Talk by Office of Sustainability & Campus Enrichment Student Interns.

This event will take place via zoom, click the link below to register.
data.description: This talk examines the importance of integrating logistics and collaboration within the planning stages of humanitarian efforts to generate long-lasting, efficient action. By analyzing the potential risk of certain international development projects and the different factors that influence their success, we challenge listeners to take on a perspective that questions the effectiveness of such investments; one that considers whether a focus on sustainability development and ethical motives can generate a more consolidated-regarding materials and funding- yet efficacious and a qualitative result that benefits all societies, economies, and environments involved.

data.title: Could A Robot Be Your Next Door Neighbor?
data.summary:
Campus Sustainability Month Talk by Office of Sustainability & Campus Enrichment Student Interns.

This event will take place via zoom, click the link below to register.
data.description: As the artificial intelligence industry grows, data center developments built by hyperscalers are rapidly expanding into residential backyards, creating environmental and socioeconomic strains for nearby communities. These mega-facilities consume vast resources—generating heavy upfront carbon emissions from concrete and steel construction while exacerbating local air, water, and noise pollution during operation. Furthermore, their power demands strain regional electricity grids, driving up residential utility bills and threatening power reliability. Addressing these localized community impacts requires corporate sustainability disclosures, global and local AI governance, and collaborative policy frameworks.

data.title: Understanding Food Deserts: Barriers, Opportunity, and Access
data.summary:
Campus Sustainability Month Talk by Office of Sustainability & Campus Enrichment Student Interns.

This event will take place via zoom, click the link below to register.
data.description: Access to healthy and affordable food remains a challenge for many communities across the United States. Learn about the issue of food deserts, why they exist, and how they affect individuals and communities. Discover the connection between food access, nutrition, and overall well-being, as well as potential solutions to create a more accessible and sustainable food system.
